Mode.Name: How Intelligence buys proficiencies
Mode.Hint: The rule as written gives a number of proficiencies equal to the Intelligence modifier, each costing one. The Intellect Points variant gives that many points instead, and a skill costs two of them while a tool, weapon or language costs one.
Mode.Points: Intellect Points — a skill costs two

Minimum.Name: Least a character may have
Minimum.Hint: A floor under the budget, for a table that does not want a low-Intelligence character to get nothing. Leave at 0 to follow the rule exactly.

Sheet.None: No Intelligence proficiencies — this character's Intelligence modifier is not positive.
Sheet.Tooltip: A positive Intelligence modifier grants extra proficiencies (skills, tools or languages). Click to choose them.

Picker.Title: Intelligence Proficiencies — {name}
Picker.Search: Search skills, tools, weapons and languages…
Picker.HintFlat: Your Intelligence modifier is how many of these you may take. Each one costs one.
Picker.HintPoints: Your Intelligence modifier is how many Intellect Points you have. A skill costs two; a tool, weapon or language costs one — those may need the GM's approval.
